issues.message: Onboarding can begin immediately after the offer or salary negotiation, with no activity representing acceptance of the offer.
issues.suggestion: Add an offer-acceptance step or decision before either path can begin onboarding.

issues.message: The process ends after paperwork, orientation, and training without modeling that the new hire is fully integrated into the team.
issues.suggestion: Add and require a final integration outcome before the end event.

issues.message: After a candidate completes either the virtual or in-person interview, ExclusiveGateway_2 can route back via SequenceFlow_20 to ExclusiveGateway_1, which re-selects between virtual and in-person interview again. This contradicts the description's stated rule that a candidate is invited to in-person OR virtual interview depending on their single preference — the loop allows the same candidate to be routed through the interview-selection decision repeatedly rather than making a one-time choice.
issues.suggestion: Remove the loop-back flow SequenceFlow_20, or add an explicit condition/state ensuring the interview-type decision is made only once per candidate before proceeding to Choose candidate.

issues.message: The reference states onboarding begins 'after the offer is accepted,' implying the offer could be declined, but the diagram has no branch after Extend offer / ExclusiveGateway_6 representing offer rejection or withdrawal — every path from Task_8 eventually leads to onboarding (Task_4) regardless of candidate response.
issues.suggestion: Add a decision after Extend offer for offer acceptance vs. rejection, routing rejected offers to an alternate path (e.g., back to Choose candidate or process end) instead of unconditionally proceeding to onboarding.

issues.message: The semester-repeat loop (ExclusiveGateway_11 -> SequenceFlow_56 -> ExclusiveGateway_9 -> Task_26 'Begin attending classes') re-enters the process directly at 'Begin attending classes' for each subsequent semester, bypassing 'Meet with academic advisor' (Task_9), 'Select courses' (Task_24), and 'Resolve schedule conflicts' (Task_11). The reference states the process repeats each semester until graduation or withdrawal, and explicitly lists course selection as part of that recurring cycle, so a returning student has no path to select courses for the new semester.
issues.suggestion: Route the semester-repeat branch (SequenceFlow_56) back through the course-selection sequence (Task_9 -> Task_24 -> Task_11) before merging into 'Begin attending classes', rather than looping directly to ExclusiveGateway_9.

issues.message: The description states subcomponents are tested individually right after each is built, but the diagram only routes to testing (ServiceTask_1..4 via ParallelGateway_1) after the entire 'build next subcomponent' loop (controlled by the 'Parts remained?' gateway) has completed. All subcomponents are built first, then tested together in a batch, contradicting the explicit build-then-test-per-subcomponent order.
issues.suggestion: Move the individual test activity (or a per-subcomponent test gateway) to occur immediately after each 'Build the next subcomponent' iteration, rather than batching all tests after the build loop exits.

issues.message: The reference description defines a conditional returns process triggered when the customer reports issues upon delivery (return shipping label, receiving returned items, inspection, refund/replacement), but the diagram contains no branch, gateway, or activities implementing this scenario. After 'Confirm delivery' and 'Send follow-up email', the flow proceeds unconditionally toward the end event with no decision point for delivery issues.
issues.suggestion: Add a gateway after 'Confirm delivery' that checks whether the customer reported an issue; if so, route to a returns sub-process covering sending a return shipping label, receiving returned items, inspecting them, and processing a refund or replacement, before merging back to process completion.

However, the reference explicitly describes a returns process that must trigger when the customer reports issues upon delivery (return shipping label, receiving returned items, inspection, and refund/replacement), and this entire conditional path is absent from the model: after 'Confirm delivery' and 'Send follow-up email' the flow proceeds unconditionally to the end event with no branch or activity representing the returns scenario.", "result": {"findings": [{"category": "missing_exception_handling", "classification_basis": "required_scenario_path_absent", "severity": "warning", "message": "The reference description defines a conditional returns process triggered when the customer reports issues upon delivery (return shipping label, receiving returned items, inspection, refund/replacement), but the diagram contains no branch, gateway, or activities implementing this scenario. After 'Confirm delivery' and 'Send follow-up email', the flow proceeds unconditionally toward the end event with no decision point for delivery issues.", "element_refs": ["Task_2", "Task_22", "ExclusiveGateway_12", "ExclusiveGateway_1"], "reference_evidence": ["L17", "L18", "L19", "L20", "L21"], "suggestion": "Add a gateway after 'Confirm delivery' that checks whether the customer reported an issue; if so, route to a returns sub-process covering sending a return shipping label, receiving returned items, inspecting them, and processing a refund or replacement, before merging back to process completion."}]}}

issues.message: ExclusiveGateway_1's outgoing flow SequenceFlow_15 is guarded by condition '${refinementNotRequired}' yet it routes to Task_5 'Refine prototype', while the unconditioned flow SequenceFlow_16 routes to the approve/discard decision (ExclusiveGateway_3). This inverts the stated rule: refinement should occur only when needed, and testing should be reinitiated in that case, but as modeled the 'refinement needed' scenario cannot select the branch that performs refinement because that branch's guard states the opposite condition.
issues.suggestion: Swap the condition expressions (or their targets) so that the flow guarded by 'refinement needed' leads to Task_5 'Refine prototype', and the flow guarded by 'refinement not required' leads to ExclusiveGateway_3 (approve/discard).

issues.message: ParallelGateway_3 splits the testing phase into three parallel branches intended to cover functionality, safety, and market potential (per the reference). Task_6 'Test functionality' and Task_11 'Evaluate product functionality' both address functionality, duplicating each other, while no branch addresses safety, even though a node occupies that third structural test position.
issues.suggestion: Rename Task_11 (or its role) to reflect a safety assessment, e.g. 'Assess prototype safety', so all three required test dimensions (functionality, safety, market potential) are represented.

issues.message: The reference requires the ticket to be sent to the customer via email or SMS, but the exclusive gateway ExclusiveGateway_7 that is supposed to choose between the two delivery channels routes to two tasks that both perform email delivery (Task_13 'Deliver ticket by email' and Task_2 'Send ticket via email'). The branch that should represent SMS delivery instead duplicates the email behavior, so the SMS scenario described in the reference is never actually modeled.
issues.suggestion: Rename/rebehave one of the two outgoing branches of ExclusiveGateway_7 (e.g. Task_2) to represent an actual SMS delivery activity, distinct from the email delivery already performed by Task_13.

calls.output: {"description": "The process largely matches the reference narrative (search → select route/date/time → provide personal & payment info → generate ticket → update inventory & deliver ticket → optional reminders/instructions → optional post-travel feedback → end). One semantic defect was found: the reference states the ticket is sent \"via email or SMS\", but the exclusive gateway offering the two delivery alternatives (ExclusiveGateway_7) routes to two tasks that both perform email delivery (Task_13 \"Deliver ticket by email\" and Task_2 \"Send ticket via email\"), so the SMS alternative described in the reference is never actually represented — the second branch occupies the SMS role but is mislabeled/implemented as email again.", "result": {"findings": [{"category": "inconsistent_naming", "classification_basis": "label_or_behavior_mismatch", "severity": "warning", "message": "The reference requires the ticket to be sent to the customer via email or SMS, but the exclusive gateway ExclusiveGateway_7 that is supposed to choose between the two delivery channels routes to two tasks that both perform email delivery (Task_13 'Deliver ticket by email' and Task_2 'Send ticket via email'). The branch that should represent SMS delivery instead duplicates the email behavior, so the SMS scenario described in the reference is never actually modeled.", "element_refs": ["ExclusiveGateway_7", "Task_13", "Task_2"], "reference_evidence": ["L3"], "suggestion": "Rename/rebehave one of the two outgoing branches of ExclusiveGateway_7 (e.g. Task_2) to represent an actual SMS delivery activity, distinct from the email delivery already performed by Task_13."}]}}

issues.message: After turning on the printer, the model waits for status and checks whether it is heated, but never models heating the bed and extruder.
issues.suggestion: Add a task to heat the printer bed and extruder after turning on the printer, with status monitoring continuing until heating is complete.

issues.message: The reference states that after being satisfied with the artist's result, the user must choose a plastic color for printing, before checking whether that color is in stock. No task represents this 'choose a plastic color' activity; the flow goes directly from the 'Satisfied with result?' gateway to the 'In stock?' gateway.
issues.suggestion: Insert an explicit 'Choose plastic color' task on SequenceFlow_30 between the 'Satisfied with result?' gateway and the 'In stock?' gateway.

issues.message: L4 states that when the machine is restarted, measuring should continue. In the diagram, ManualTask_1 'Continue measuring' does not loop back to the OEE data collection (ParallelGateway_1 / StartEvent_1); instead SequenceFlow_19 routes it to ExclusiveGateway_4/ExclusiveGateway_2 and the process terminates at EndEvent_1, the same as the 'disconnect' outcome. The scenario of resuming ongoing measurement after a restart has no represented path back into the measurement loop.
issues.suggestion: Route SequenceFlow_19 (or an added flow from ManualTask_1) back to ParallelGateway_1 / StartEvent_1 so that measurement continues after a restart, instead of merging into the same termination path used for the disconnect scenario.

In the diagram, ManualTask_1 'Continue measuring' does not loop back to the OEE data collection (ParallelGateway_1 / StartEvent_1); instead SequenceFlow_19 routes it to ExclusiveGateway_4/ExclusiveGateway_2 and the process terminates at EndEvent_1, the same as the 'disconnect' outcome. The scenario of resuming ongoing measurement after a restart has no represented path back into the measurement loop.", "element_refs": ["ManualTask_1", "SequenceFlow_19", "ExclusiveGateway_4", "EndEvent_1"], "reference_evidence": ["L4"], "suggestion": "Route SequenceFlow_19 (or an added flow from ManualTask_1) back to ParallelGateway_1 / StartEvent_1 so that measurement continues after a restart, instead of merging into the same termination path used for the disconnect scenario."}]}}

issues.message: ExclusiveGateway_1's alternate branch (SequenceFlow_20) bypasses Task_1 'Transition into new role' and merges directly at ExclusiveGateway_3 into the same EndEvent_1 used by the approved/promoted path. This allows the process to terminate without the employee being promoted and transitioning into the new role, contradicting the explicit required end state.
issues.suggestion: Model a distinct outcome/end state for the non-approved path (e.g., a separate end event or explicit 'not promoted' terminal state) so the shared end event is reached only after the promotion and transition steps, per the described final business state.

issues.message: The process creates the personal development plan (Task_2) before identifying the employee's development needs or career aspirations (Task_5), reversing the order explicitly described in the reference: identification of needs should occur first, followed by creation of the development plan.
issues.suggestion: Reorder the flow so Task_5 (Identify development needs or career aspirations) precedes Task_2 (Create personal development plan), matching the described sequence: Start -> identify needs -> create plan -> ...

issues.message: SequenceFlow_16 from ExclusiveGateway_11 leads to Task_13 'Notify about failed payment', but its condition_expression is '${paymentSucceeded}'. Per the reference, this notification should occur when payment fails, not when it succeeds, so the branch's guard prevents the explicitly required failure scenario (L4) from ever selecting this path, while the unconditional/default flow to stock checking would instead be taken on payment failure.
issues.suggestion: Change the condition on SequenceFlow_16 to something like '${!paymentSucceeded}' (or 'paymentFailed'), and ensure the flow to Task_9 (stock check) is guarded by '${paymentSucceeded}' or is the default flow.

issues.message: Sequence flow SequenceFlow_35 is labeled 'Vodka bar' and leads to SendTask_2 (Send requirements to the russian team), matching the reference mapping of vodka bar to the Russian team. However its condition_expression is '${barType == \'whiskey\'}', so the flow will actually only ever fire when the customer selected the whiskey bar, not the vodka bar. This contradicts both its own label and the adjacent 'Whiskey bar' branch (SequenceFlow_36), which has no distinguishing condition of its own.
issues.suggestion: Change the condition_expression on SequenceFlow_35 to check for the vodka bar selection (e.g. barType == 'vodka'), consistent with its label and target team.

issues.message: The reference states the test protocol created during the flight is sent to both 'you' (the manufacturer) and the customer. The diagram only models sending the protocol to the customer (SendTask_7 'Send protocol to customer'); no activity or flow represents sending/retaining the protocol internally.
issues.suggestion: Add a task or flow that sends/records the flight protocol internally (to the manufacturer), alongside the existing send to the customer.

issues.message: The “Yes” path from “Is in stock?” withdraws the product even though its condition is `${productOutOfStock}`.
issues.suggestion: Make the withdrawal path selectable only when the product is in stock, and route the out-of-stock condition to reordering.

issues.message: When the order is not ready for shipment, the flow loops directly to the stock check without selecting the next product.
issues.suggestion: Add a task to select the next product between the “No” shipment-ready branch and the repeated stock check.

flow_nodes.name: Check if product is in stock
Demand delivery delay penalty from the wholesaler
Check if the whole order is ready for shipment
Arrived after more than ten days?

issues.message: The 'Is in stock?' gateway's 'Yes' flow to 'Withdraw the Product from warehouse' carries the condition_expression '${productOutOfStock}', which is the opposite of what 'Yes' (in stock) should require. Per L4, when the product is in stock it must be withdrawn from the warehouse, but with this condition the 'Yes' branch only evaluates true when the product is actually out of stock, so for the true in-stock scenario this branch cannot be selected and execution instead falls through to the 'No'/reorder branch.
issues.suggestion: Correct the condition_expression on SequenceFlow_4 to something like '${!productOutOfStock}' (or 'productInStock') so the in-stock scenario actually triggers the withdrawal path, matching the 'Yes' label.

issues.message: L10 explicitly states that when the order is not yet ready for shipment, 'the next product from the order is selected' before the process restarts the stock check. The diagram's 'No' loop (SequenceFlow_16) from 'Order is ready for shipment?' goes directly back into the merge gateway before 'Check if product is in stock' with no activity representing selection of the next product from the order.
issues.suggestion: Insert a task (e.g. 'Select next product from order') on the SequenceFlow_16 loop-back path before it reaches ExclusiveGateway_5/ServiceTask_2.

issues.message: After the customer submits a cancellation request, the flow immediately splits into financial handling and completion; it contains no task for the support team to process the request.
issues.suggestion: Add a support-team cancellation-processing task after the request and before the subsequent cancellation activities.

issues.message: The process can reach the end event without a subscription-deactivation activity, including after final balance settlement and through the direct path from the cancellation decision.
issues.suggestion: Model subscription deactivation by the support team and require it before the end event.

issues.message: After the customer-cancels decision (ExclusiveGateway_1 -> SequenceFlow_9 -> ExclusiveGateway_3), ExclusiveGateway_3 offers a second, unlabeled outgoing path (SequenceFlow_17) that goes directly to ExclusiveGateway_2 and the end event, bypassing 'Customer submits cancellation request' (Task_2), the charge/refund decision, and 'Settle final account balance' (Task_7). This contradicts the explicit required order: cancellation request -> support team processing -> refunds/charges -> settlement.
issues.suggestion: Remove the direct SequenceFlow_17 escape from ExclusiveGateway_3, or clearly label it as a scenario the reference does not describe; ensure every cancellation path routes through request submission, charge/refund handling and balance settlement.

issues.message: The reference states the process concludes when the subscription is deactivated by the support team AND the final account balance is settled. The diagram only models 'Settle final account balance' (Task_7) before merging at ParallelGateway_6/ExclusiveGateway_2 and ending; no activity anywhere in the diagram represents deactivating the subscription, so every completed run reaches EndEvent_1 without that required final business state.
issues.suggestion: Add a 'Deactivate subscription' activity (e.g., performed by the support team) on the cancellation path before or alongside settling the final balance and prior to the shared end event.

issues.message: The reference requires that when a customer reports issues upon delivery, a returns process (send return label, receive returned items, inspect them, process refund/replacement) is initiated. The diagram has no such branch: after Task_2 'Confirm delivery' and Task_22 'Send follow-up email', flow passes unconditionally through ExclusiveGateway_12 and ExclusiveGateway_10 straight to EndEvent_1, with no path modeling reported delivery issues or any return-handling activities.
issues.suggestion: Add a decision after delivery confirmation (e.g. at ExclusiveGateway_12 or a new gateway) branching on whether the customer reports an issue; model the returns sub-path with tasks for sending a return shipping label, receiving returned items, inspecting them, and processing a refund or replacement before reaching the end event.

However, the returns process explicitly required by the reference description (L17-L21) for the case where the customer reports delivery issues is entirely absent from the model: after 'Confirm delivery' / 'Send follow-up email' the flow passes straight through two single-in/single-out exclusive gateways to the end event with no branch, no return-shipping-label activity, no receipt/inspection of returned items, and no refund/replacement processing.", "result": {"findings": [{"category": "missing_exception_handling", "classification_basis": "required_scenario_path_absent", "severity": "warning", "message": "The reference requires that when a customer reports issues upon delivery, a returns process (send return label, receive returned items, inspect them, process refund/replacement) is initiated. The diagram has no such branch: after Task_2 'Confirm delivery' and Task_22 'Send follow-up email', flow passes unconditionally through ExclusiveGateway_12 and ExclusiveGateway_10 straight to EndEvent_1, with no path modeling reported delivery issues or any return-handling activities.", "element_refs": ["Task_2", "Task_22", "ExclusiveGateway_12", "ExclusiveGateway_10", "EndEvent_1"], "reference_evidence": ["L17", "L18", "L19", "L20", "L21"], "suggestion": "Add a decision after delivery confirmation (e.g. at ExclusiveGateway_12 or a new gateway) branching on whether the customer reports an issue; model the returns sub-path with tasks for sending a return shipping label, receiving returned items, inspecting them, and processing a refund or replacement before reaching the end event."}]}}

issues.message: Exclusive gateway 'All tests successfull?' (ExclusiveGateway_5) has only one outgoing sequence flow (SequenceFlow_21, labeled 'Yes') leading to assembly. There is no outgoing flow representing an unsuccessful test outcome, so the explicitly described failure scenario ('If subcomponents are not tested successfully, you have to redesign and rebuild them') has no corresponding path back to the design/build activities (e.g. UserTask_1 or ManualTask_3).
issues.suggestion: Add a 'No' outgoing flow from ExclusiveGateway_5 that routes back to the redesign step (UserTask_1 'Develop basic design') or to rebuilding the affected subcomponent (ManualTask_3 'Build the next subcomponent') when tests fail.

issues.message: The reference requires the parallel risk assessment to cover financial, operational, and compliance risks (L9). ParallelGateway_1 fans out to three tasks: 'Evaluate financial risks' (Task_14), 'Evaluate compliance risks' (Task_13), and 'Assess financial exposure' (Task_24). The third branch, which occupies the structural slot for operational-risk evaluation, is labeled and effectively duplicates a financial-risk activity instead of representing operational risk, so operational risk is never actually evaluated even though a node exists in that position.
issues.suggestion: Rename Task_24 (or replace it) to reflect an operational risk evaluation activity, e.g. 'Evaluate operational risks', so all three risk categories from L9 are represented and not duplicated.

issues.message: The reference requires notifying both Social Security and the Company. The process has two parallel notification tasks after 'prepare necessary documents for leave' (ManualTask_2 and ManualTask_3), but both are labeled as notifying the social security / social-insurance office ('Notify social-insurance office' and 'notify social security'), which are the same recipient under different names. No task represents notifying the Company/employer, even though the structural slot (the second parallel branch) exists for it.
issues.suggestion: Rename ManualTask_2 (or ManualTask_3) to reflect notifying the Company/employer instead of duplicating the Social Security notification.

flow_nodes.name: check if all necessary documents gathered
decide if extend leave or return to work
decide if apply for financial support

issues.message: For the more-than-one-hour branch, the task is labelled “go to home,” whereas the required behavior is to go to the event from home.
issues.suggestion: Rename and model this task as going to the Night Run from home.

issues.message: The branch for one hour or less proceeds directly to the run; it contains no activity for leaving directly from work.
issues.suggestion: Add an activity for leaving directly from work on the “No” branch before the running activities.

issues.message: The parallel Night Run section models running, pace recording, and time measurement, but no drinking activity.
issues.suggestion: Add a drinking activity in parallel with running and join it before receiving the final time.

issues.message: The reference states that during the Night Run 'you run and drink at the same time', implying a concurrent drinking activity alongside running. The parallel split after ExclusiveGateway_4 (ParallelGateway_3) only branches into 'run' (ManualTask_4), 'Record running pace' (ManualTask_5) and 'measure the time' (ServiceTask_4); no task represents drinking.
issues.suggestion: Add a parallel 'drink' task branching from ParallelGateway_3 (and merging back into ParallelGateway_4) alongside the running and measurement tasks.

issues.message: The reference explicitly states that if less than one hour remains before the end of the workday, the participant must 'leave directly from work'. In the diagram, the 'No' branch of ExclusiveGateway_3 ('time more than 1 hour?') flows straight into ExclusiveGateway_4 with no task representing this required leaving-from-work activity, unlike the 'Yes' branch which has an explicit 'go to home' task.
issues.suggestion: Insert a 'leave directly from work' task on the 'No' outgoing flow of ExclusiveGateway_3, mirroring the 'go to home' task on the 'Yes' branch.

issues.message: The flow from Tell artist to change loops back through the gateway into Send sketches to an artist again, resending sketches on every revision iteration, contradicting the described one-time send followed by iterative change requests until satisfied.
issues.suggestion: Route the change-request flow back to Receive result instead of Send sketches to an artist.

The diagram has no 'order finished' activity anywhere; after ParallelGateway_2 merges the payment-confirmation and address branches, the flow goes straight through ExclusiveGateway_5 to EndEvent_1 'Close E-Shop Homepage', which only represents closing the shop UI, not the required business outcome of the order being finished.

issues.message: There is no path to send the additional message when an expansion is released; the process ends after the initial confirmation and selfies.
issues.suggestion: Add a conditional/event-driven path for an expansion release that sends the additional message.

issues.message: The reference states that, in addition to receiving a confirmation and character selfies, the user gets another message as soon as an expansion is released. The diagram only models 'Receive confirmation' (ServiceTask_3) and 'Receive character selfies' (ServiceTask_4) merging into the end event; there is no activity or conditional path representing the expansion-release notification.
issues.suggestion: Add a conditional path or event (e.g. an intermediate/end message event 'Expansion released notification') after or alongside ServiceTask_3/ServiceTask_4 to represent the expansion-release message.

issues.message: After ExclusiveGateway_6 ('Name available?') resolves to 'Yes', flow SequenceFlow_41 leads to Task_1 which is again labeled 'Enter character name' — duplicating the exact same activity already performed at UserTask_11 before the availability check. Per the description, names are entered one by one only until one is available; once available, the process should proceed (e.g., to confirmation), not re-enter the same name.
issues.suggestion: Rename Task_1 to reflect its actual role (e.g. 'Confirm selected character name') or remove it if entering the name already occurred at UserTask_11.

issues.message: On the failure branch of gateway 'All tests successfull?' (SequenceFlow_30), the process routes to Task_1 'Assemble subcomponents' before looping back to redesign. Assembly is explicitly permitted only when all tests succeed (the Yes branch, handled by ManualTask_5), while the reference states that failed tests must trigger a redesign/rebuild instead of assembly.
issues.suggestion: Replace Task_1 on the 'No' path with a distinct 'Redesign and rebuild subcomponents' activity instead of reusing the 'Assemble subcomponents' action that belongs to the success path.

issues.message: On the 'Yes' (issue fixed) branch of gateway 'Is issue fixed?', flow SequenceFlow_45 leads into Task_1 'Send device to an expert' before continuing to the review/video questions. Per the reference, sending the device to an expert is explicitly the action for when the repair 'hasn't worked out' (the opposite, 'No' branch, already correctly leads to ManualTask_2 'Send device to an expert'). Performing this same action again on the success path is a prohibited action for that condition.
issues.suggestion: Remove or relabel Task_1 on the 'Yes' branch so that a successfully fixed device flows directly into the 'Have intention to write a review?' gateway without an unnecessary/contradictory 'send to expert' step.
